headline: Bluff Definition: Vocabulary and Reading for ESL
problemStatement: Knowing a word includes more than recognizing its spelling; learners need to understand how a definition sounds and what details make it convincing. Bluff Definition gives students a secret word, asks them to invent a dictionary-style meaning, and invites the class to separate the real definition from the bluffs.
outcomes: Practice paraphrasing a word's meaning in clear, concise language.
Read several definitions closely and notice details that make an explanation plausible.
Use vocabulary knowledge to identify a true meaning and create a convincing decoy.
howItWorks: The activity presents a secret word and its real definition. Students write fake definitions on their phones without copying the actual meaning.
The teacher combines the submissions with the real definition and asks students to vote for the meaning they believe is correct.
A student who already knows the real meaning can use the dedicated option instead of adding another fake. Students cannot earn points by voting for their own definition.
Identical fake definitions are grouped together, and the results highlight successful bluffers. The teacher can read a response aloud and ask what made it sound real.
teacherUseCases: Use a recent vocabulary word when students need practice paraphrasing rather than repeating a memorized dictionary entry.
After the result, discuss which clues helped the class distinguish the real definition and which invented details were persuasive.

faq.q: What if students already know the word?
faq.a: They can select the already-knew-it option for credit rather than writing a false definition. This keeps a correct real meaning out of the bluff choices.

faq.q: Can students vote for their own fake definition?
faq.a: No. Votes for a student's own option are ignored, so points come from convincing other classmates instead of selecting one's own response.
Matching fake definitions are merged into one choice, and the students who wrote that wording share the associated points.

faq.q: What speaking activity follows the vote?
faq.a: The results highlight the best bluffer, and the teacher can read a definition aloud and ask why it sounded believable. Students explain language choices, not just scores.
